notes:
Lead source: organic inbound from blog post about prompt engineering. SMB, seed-funded, building customer support assistant + semantic search. Currently using Hosted API (open Llama-2-13B variant) via self-serve; latency good, but token costs spiking. Primary asks:
- Token usage audit across last 7 days and high-level cost breakdown by route (chat vs embeddings)
- Practical recommendations for batching/caching (prefix KV caching, response chunking)
- Prompt compression tactics: shorter system messages, template variables, instruction deduping, compressing context, and use of compact serialization for metadata
- Guidance on batching: when to batch vs stream for UX tradeoffs, recommended batch sizes for 20 QPS peak, expected latency impact and cost savings estimates
- Recommendations for token budgeting and tooling to track expensive prompts (alerts, per-route cost dashboards)
- Quick wins (low lift): trim system prompts, reuse cached embeddings, reduce context window to active span, apply prompt templates and param substitution, evaluate model quantization suggestions from Optimize
- Longer-term: consider prefix caching + reranking to reduce generative tokens for search; potential Dedicated later if throughput demands grow
Concise requirements: avg response latency target ~<300ms, peak throughput ~20 QPS, strict cost sensitivity (want <$0.01 per typical support reply). Security: needs SSO (Okta) and SOC2 evidence before procurement.
Quotes: "Latency's great, but bills are unpredictable - need concrete levers to bring costs down without breaking UX."
Open items: sample token audit (requested); decision on pursuing Redwood Optimize add-on; legal/security to review SOC2 artifact.
Next steps: run token audit, produce 1-page cost-optimization checklist (batching/caching, prompt compression, token budgeting), then 30m follow-up call to review findings (week of 2026-02-24).
